exercise.name: Barbell Lying Seal Row on Rack
aliases: Prone wide barbell row on a high bench

reference.title: Barbell Lying Seal Row on Rack
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the bar comes up to the bench, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: the chest stays on the pad and the bar touches the bench each rep.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep touches the bench with a pause.

cues.text: Lie face down on a high flat bench inside a rack, chin past the end, legs straight; overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders, arms hanging long just above the pins.
Lead with the elbows out to the sides and pull the bar up to the underside of the bench.
Touch the bench and squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly until the arms are long, without touching the pins.
Stay flat; start the next rep from a dead hang.

mistakes.mistake: Kicking the legs or arching off the bench
mistakes.fix: Stay flat and strict: no body English.
Touch the bench every rep and straighten the arms at the bottom.
Pull the shoulder blades back, not up.
For a seal row, lead with the elbows out at about 60-75 degrees from the trunk.

kinematics.norm: Chest-supported rows remove most of the lower-back load of a bent-over row (Fenwick 2009 compared rowing exercises)
Wide grip and flared elbows bias the rear deltoid and mid back (Schoenfeld 2013)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Set up the bench so it cannot tip, and the safety pins so the bar is easy to reach and to set down.
Climb on and off the high bench carefully; have the bar on the pins while you get set.
Shoulder pain: narrow the grip and keep the elbows closer to the body.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Lower bench and lighter plates if the arms cannot hang.
progressions: Pause with the bar on the bench.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Extends the shoulder; with the elbows out it shares the work with the upper back.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Extends the shoulder; with the elbows out it shares the work with the upper back.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together as the bar meets the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together as the bar meets the bench.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Flared elbows put the rear shoulders to work.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Flared elbows put the rear shoulders to work.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the upper arm turned out.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the upper arm turned out.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder blades; no shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder blades; no shrug.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the body flat on the bench.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk long; the bench takes the load off the lower back.
